eMudScan now updates itself, and its fixes are scripts that you can read before you run them.

### Highlights

- **Updates.** eMudScan now tells you when a new version is out, shows its release notes, then downloads, checks and installs it for you. [How updates work](https://github.com/3c0/eMudScan/blob/4.0.0/docs/using.md#updates)
- **Fixes you can read.** Each fix is now a script with comments, and shows the result of each command: you see what it changes before you run it, and what it did after. [Fixing software](https://github.com/3c0/eMudScan/blob/4.0.0/docs/using.md#fixing-software)
- **Up-to-date fixes.** The fix of a Python or a node.exe inside a program now downloads the latest release of its line, which eMudScan looks for when the Fix window opens.
- **Keyboard.** You can now reach every control and every link with Tab. [Keyboard shortcuts](https://github.com/3c0/eMudScan/blob/4.0.0/docs/using.md#keyboard-shortcuts)

### Also in this version

- In the Fix window, you can click `check_ssl.py` to read and copy the tests that the fix of a Python runs.
- For a Python inside a program, the detailed information gives a script that you can run yourself, without eMudScan.
- The fixes also run on a PC without Windows PowerShell, in PowerShell 7.
- The reports give the result of each fix, without the commands.
- The detailed information and the About box are easier to read, and the windows are wider.
- The mouse pointer shows when eMudScan is busy, and **Copy report** says **Copied**.
- You can type in the search box as soon as a scan starts.
- The mouse wheel scrolls the lists one row at a time.
- “Allow the online test” is now named “Online checks and updates”, since it also allows the updates.

### Fixed

- Ctrl+C and Ctrl+A no longer play the Windows sound when you copy or select a text.
- The fixes now work when you start eMudScan from PowerShell 7.
- Long URLs and paths are now cut between two names, not in the middle of one.
- Greyed-out buttons now show their tooltip, which says when you can use them.
- The open windows now follow a change of the display scale.
